The finite lifetime τ of a level produces a natural (lifetime) width  

 ΔE ≃ ħ ⁄ (2 τ)  (from ΔE Δt ≈ ħ⁄2).

For the two levels

1. τ₁ = 10⁻⁹ s → ΔE₁ ≃ ħ/(2τ₁)  
  = (6.58 × 10⁻¹⁶ eV s)/(2 × 10⁻⁹ s) ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁷ eV

2. τ₂ = 10⁻⁸ s → ΔE₂ ≃ ħ/(2τ₂)  
  = (6.58 × 10⁻¹⁶ eV s)/(2 × 10⁻⁸ s) ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁸ eV

The combined natural width that blurs the two lines is therefore of order  

 ΔE₁ + ΔE₂ ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁷ eV + 3 × 10⁻⁸ eV ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁷ eV.

To “clearly distinguish” (resolve) the two levels, their energy separation must exceed this total width—i.e. it should be ≳ 10⁻⁶ eV.  

Among the offered choices,

(A) 10⁻⁸ eV   too small  
(B) 10⁻⁴ eV   ≫ 10⁻⁶ eV  → adequate for clear resolution  
(C) 10⁻¹¹ eV   far too small  
(D) 10⁻⁹ eV   too small  

Hence the only value that allows unambiguous resolution is 10⁻⁴ eV.

Answer: B
